Notes: Operating_System- Introduction to OS

Introduction to OS
​​​​​​​Operating System is a System Software which creates a platform for other softwares/applications.
 It can also be called as a----
  • Interface between user and a hardware.
  • Resource allocator.
  • Program controller.
​      
​​​​​​​Let us see what System Software is...
      System software is a type of computer program that is designed to run computer's hardware and application programs. If we think of the computer system as a layered model, the system software is the interface between the hardware and user applications. The operating system is the best-known example of system software. OS manages all other programs in a computer.

Other examples of system software include the following--
  1. The BIOS (basic input/output system) :: This system software ,gets the computer system started after it's turned on and manages the data flow between the OS and attached devices, such as the hard drive, vido adapter, keyboard,mouse and printer.
  2. The boot program :: This system software loads the OS into the computer's main memory or random access memory (RAM).
  3. An assembler :: takes basic computer instructions and converts them into a pattern of bits that the processor of computer can use to perform its basic operations.
  4. A device driver ::  controls a particular type of device that is attached to your computer, such as a keyboard or mouse.
  5. Additionally, system software can also include system utilities, such as the Disk Defragmenter and System Restore, and development tools, such as Compilers and Debuggers.
​​​​​​​
Defination OS
​​​​​​​Operating System is a system software which communicates with the hardware of the system. It provides a layer between hardware and the users and works as a user interface. An Operating System (OS) is a collection of software that manages computer hardware resources and provides common services for computer programs. The operating system is the most important type of system software in a computer system. It manages all the resources of the computer.  

Hence, Operating System is  a set of specialized programs that handle all the operations of the computer. It controls and monitors the execution of all other programs that resides  in the computer, which also includes application programs and other system software of the computer. Examples of Operating Systems are Windows, Linux, Mac OS, etc.

   

Functions of OS
Following are the basic important functions which any Operating System performs 
Security
The operating system uses password protection to protect user data and similar other techniques. It also prevents unauthorized  access to programs and user data.
Resourse Managment 
    ​​​​​​​The Operating System ensures the proper use of all the resources available by deciding  which resource to be     used by whom for how much time. All the decisions are taken by the Operating System.
Process Managment
    In a multi programming environment, the OS decides the order in which processes will have access to the     
    processor, and how much processing time each process has. OS keeps track of the status of processes. 
File Managment
    A file system is organized into directories for efficient or easy navigation and usage. These directories may              contain other directories and other files. An Operating System carries out the task to store and retrive the              information. It also looks into user access settings and status of every file. 
Job accounting
   Operating system Keeps track of time and resources used by various tasks and users, this information can be         used to track resource usage for a particular user or group of user.
Error detection 
   Operating system constantly monitors the system to detect errors and avoid malfunctioning of computer               system.
Memory Managment
   The operating system manages the Primary Memory or Main Memory. Main memory is made up of a large           array of bytes or words where each byte or word is assigned a certain address. Main memory is a fast storage       and it can be accessed directly by the CPU. For a program to be executed, it should be first loaded in the main       memory. An  Operating System manages all these activities.
Coordination between S/Ws and users
   Operating systems also coordinates and assigns interpreters, compilers, assemblers and other software to the       various users of the computer systems.     

​​​​​​​​
Command Interpreter 
One of the major functions of OS is to interprete the commands. Operating systems provides an interface to the users for the communication with the  Computer. A command interpreter is a program which reads the instructions given by the user. It then translates these instructions into the context of the operating system. Command interpreter is also known as a Shell of OS. Command interprater provides a user interface to hide hardware details of the system from its users, making system more user friendly.
The two commonly used methods, provided by operating systems, for interfacing are
  1. Command line Interface (CLI)
  2. Graphical User Interface (GUI).

Some Concepts in OS
​Once any computer system starts(boots), OS software gets loaded in the RAM at fixed  address. Remaining part of memory is utilized to load user programs and other things. Keeping CUP busy , to get maximum throughput is the main objective of OS. Busy CPU will enhance the speed and will make computer system faster. Depending on this idea, OS is catagorised as follows  
1. Single-User Single-Tasking OS   

      ​  
An operating system that allows a single user to perform only one task at a time is called a Single-User Single-Tasking Operating System. Functions like printing a document, downloading images, etc., can be performed only one at a time. Examples of this include MS-DOS, Palm OS, etc. In this type of  OS ,only one application program runs on top of OS. Single user operating system is that in which one user works on one interface. In these systems only one user is active at a time. So there will be no other user interfering with the applications. And in these systems all computer resources are used by a user requests.  These systems use very  less resources and complexity of this system is less as well, hence  it is easy to maintain and debug the system . The system has a less chance to get damage , since number of requests from hardware and software is few. This is Single-User , Single-Tasking OS.
-- e.g MS-DOS, Palm OS


​
Advantage:
  • This operating system occupies less space in memory.
  • Algorithm is very simple and easy to implement.

Disadvantage:
  • Major disadvantage of this system is that, it is very slow and it fails to handle work load efficiently.
  • This OS has lot of limits and also CPU utilization is very poor , since CPU has to wait for another program to be brought  into the memory after completion of execution of  first program.
  • Can handle only one program at a time.


Hence the concept of Multiplogramming evolved in Operating System.
   
2. Multiprogramming OS

​

In MultiProgramming, more than one program gets loaded in memory along with OS. An attempt is to bring  more and more programs in the memory of  a computer so that the CPU will remain busy at any point of time. Processor switches rapidly between the programs available in the memory.
In this case , OS starts executing next job in two cases.....
    1. Program terminates
    2. Program is waiting for i/o services.
 CPU will process till the job is completed. CPU will switch to other job in case if the job goes for i/o functions or job terminates logically.
 -e.g Batch Processing system.
 Though Multiprogramming , the system actually processess only one program at a time. The switching between  programs is very fast.

3. Time Sharing OS/Multitasking

​

Here, idea is to process multiple programs simulteniously. Time slice/quantum is defined by OS.
In this case OS will switch to other job when-----
  1.  Time slice/quantum ends.
  2.  Program is waiting for i/o operations to complete.
  3.  Program terminates.  
Multiple programs are brought into the memory. In ideal case, CPU will process each program for definite time quantum  and then  switch to the other program. This switching is very fast and though only one program is executed at any point of time, the user gets the effect, that multiple programs are running in parallel. The CPU is never idle and is utilized to its optimum capacity. This type of a system requires extra h/w called as a Timer.  Since multiple programs reside in computer's memory, switching between the programs is faster and also CPU remains constantly busy. This increases the speed and throughput of the system.

4. Multiprocessing Operating System

​
In operating systems, to improve the performance of more than one CPU can be used within one computer system called as Multiprocessor operating system.
Multiple CPUs are interconnected so that a job can be divided among them for faster execution. When a job finishes, results from all CPUs are collected and compiled to give the final output. Jobs needed to share main memory and they may also share other system resources among themselves. Multiple CPUs can also be used to run multiple jobs simultaneously.
    
For Example: UNIX Operating system is one of the most widely used multiprocessing systems.

To enforce a multiprocessing operating system effectively, the computer system must have the following things
  • A motherboard ,capable of handling multiple processors in a multiprocessing operating system.
  • Processors , also capable of being used in a multiprocessing system.
Advantages of multiprocessing operating system   
  • Increased reliability: Due to the multiprocessing system, processing tasks can be distributed among several processors. This increases reliability as if one processor fails, the task can be given to another processor for completion.
  • Increased throughout: As several processors increase, more work can be done in less time.
  • The economy of Scale: As multiprocessors systems share peripherals, secondary storage devices, and power supplies, they are relatively cheaper than single-processor systems.
Disadvantages of Multiprocessing operating System  
  • Operating system of multiprocessing is more complex and sophisticated as it takes care of multiple CPUs at the same time.     
Understanding Memory in computer system
 Memory can be broadly catagorised as--     
​​​​​​​1. Temporary Memory

​

  • This type of memory , as the name says is temporary. Storage is not permanent.
  • The data in this memory will be cleared if system shuts down or there is a power-cut.
  • Since the memory is erased due to power failure , it is called as Volatile memory.
  • All the processing is done in this memory. 
  • Though it is temporary memory, it has very important role to play in the computer system. All the processing and loading of OS is done in this memory.
  • CPU can directly access this memory.
      e.g 
   - RAM(Random Access Memory)
   - RAM is also called as main/base memory.
2. Premanent Memory

​
-This type of memory , as the name says is permanent. Data stored stays permanent and need to be   deleted explicitly .
-If the data is to be processed from this memory, it is brought into RAM for processing.
e.g
      - ROM (Read Only Memory).
      -All important programs ,required to start the computer system are stored in ROM.

Concept of Kernel


​

Kernel is said to be the "Heart of OS". A kernel is the core component of an operating system which performs all major tasks which we classify as the functions of Operating System. System calls are handled by Kernel. It is the first program to get loaded in memory. It runs till system shuts down. It talks to h/w of the system and most important , it " Handles interrupts ". Call given to the kernel is called as System Call.

Types of Kernels 
1. Monolithic Kernel 

​

Every time when computer system gets started(boots), OS gets loaded in the memory. Some
defined memory space is reserved for kernel. When, entire / most of the OS programs reside
in  kernel space it is called as Monolithic Kernel. This Kernel is said to be a Bulkey kernel, as all the programs reside in the same memory space as that of kernel. But lesser switching between the program space is required since all programs share same memory space. Also
User services and kernel services are in same space.   
e.g UNIX
2. MicroKernel 
Microkernel is the one in which user services and kernel services are kept in separate address space. In this type of Kernel, more switching is required. But the Kernel is less bulkey .
e.g Mac OS

​
​​​​​​​Operating System Structure    
  •  Simple Structure                  DOS
  •  Monolithic                            UNIX       
  •  Microkernel                          Mac
  •  Object orianted kernel       Linux, Solaris Unix,Windows
Interrupt Handling Mechanism
Signal generated by hardware or software when a process or an event needs immediate attention  is called as Interrupt.  The signal informs the processor about a high priority and urgent information demand causing an interruption in the current working process.
e.g In a simple C code, interrupt is handled in following way...
#include<stdio.h>
int main()
{
   printf("Hello World");                                                            /* i/o call. interrupt generated
}
------------------Handled by kernel---------------------------
interrupt called                              
                             write()                                                            /*accesses o/p device
end
Interrupt Instructions work in 2 modes 
  1.  User Mode          mode bit 1
  2.  Kernel Modr        mode bit 0
Types of interrupts 
1. S/W Interrupts
    Interrupts generated through software.
    e.g  Divide by zero.
            Other  Exceptions in your program.
2. H/W Interrupts
    Interrupts generated through hardware.
    e.g Timer
 
Whenever an interrupt occurs, it causes the CPU to stop executing the current program.  Then the control is given  to  interrupt handler or interrupt service routine(ISR).
The steps in which ISR handles interrupts are as follows ::
Step 1 
     Consider that a processor is executing i'th instruction. Program counter is ponting  to the next instruction (i+1)th.
Step 2
     When an interrupt occurs the program value is stored on the process stack and the program counter is loaded with the address of interrupt service routine.
Step 3
     Once the interrupt service routine is completed the address on the process stack is popped and placed back in the program counter.
Step 4
     Now, it resumes the execution from (i+1)th line.    
​​​​​​API(application program interface)
An application programming interface (API) is code that enables two software programs to communicate. An API defines how a developer should request services from an operating system (OS) or other application, and expose data within different contexts and across multiple channels.
Any data can be shared with an application programming interface. APIs are implemented by function calls composed of verbs and nouns, the required syntax is described in the documentation of the application being called. For example, on a real estate website, one API might publish available real estate properties by geography, while a second API provides current interest rates and a third offers a mortgage calculator.
In the early days of Web 2.0, the concept of integrating data and applications from different sources was called a mashup. The web, software designed to exchange data via the internet and cloud computing have all combined to increase the interest in APIs and services.
3 Most common APIs are
  1.  Windows 32 API
  2.  POSIX  for Linux
  3.  JAVA
Types of OS
Though the basic functionalities of any operating system are same , OS can be designed as per the requirement of user. Operating System in any college lab will be different than the Operaing System used to develope any robot. With increasing demand in AI and varied requirements, design of OS may change.
Following is rough catagarization of the types of OS.
1. Batch Operating System  
​.

In Batch operating system there is no interaction between user and the computer. Firstly, user prepares his job using punch cards. Then, he submits the job to the computer operator. Operator collects the jobs from different users and sort the jobs into batches with similar needs. Jobs are batched together by type of languages and requirement. Then, operator submits the batches to the processor one by one.  All the jobs of one batch are executed together.  Multiple users can share the batch systems.
Advantages  
  • It is easy to manage large work repeatedly done.
  • It saves the time that was being wasted earlier for each individual process in context switching from one environment to another environment.
  • No manual intervention is needed.
Disadvantages 
  • All the jobs of a batch are executed sequentially one after the other.
  • The output is obtained only after all the jobs are executed.Thus, priority can not be implemented if a certain job has to be executed on an urgent basis.
  • The computer operators should be well known with batch systems.
  • Batch systems are hard to debug.
  • It is sometime costly.
  • Some times the idle time in batch system is very high due to external machine speed . The other jobs will have to wait for an unknown time if any job in the batch fails.
  • It is very difficult to guess or know the time required by any job to complete.
  • Batch operating system may lead to starvation.
  • CPU may remain idle for a long time.
Imp 
Once a batch is submitted for execution, the user is not able to interact with any of his jobs. If a job requires the user to input data during run time, then user must wait till the other jobs of the batch get executed.
This also increases the overall execution time.
Examples  
Payroll System 
Bank Statements etc
2. Time-sharing Operating System 
A time sharing system allows many users to share the computer resources simultaneously. The time sharing system provides the direct access to a large number of users where CPU time is divided among all the users on scheduled basis. The OS allocates a set of time to each user called as  time slice/time quantam. When this time is expired, it passes control to the next user on the system. The time allowed is extremely small and the user gets the impression that they each have their own CPU and they are the sole owner of the CPU​

Advantages  
Each task gets an equal opportunity.
CPU idle time can be reduced.
Multiple programs can be executed.

Disadvantages 
One must  take care of security and integrity of user programs and data.   
3. Distributed Operating System 

​

Distributed means data is stored and processed at multiple locations. Distributed systems comprises of many computers that are inter connected by communication  networks.
Advantage 

  • With resource sharing facility user at one site may be able to use the resources available at another site.
  • Speedy exchange of data with one another via electronic mail.
  • If one site fails in a distributed system, the remaining sites can potentially continue operating.
  • Better service to the customers.   

Disadvantage 

  • Security problem due to sharing.
  • Some messages can be lost in the network system.
  • Bandwidth is another problem if there is large data then all network wires to be replaced which tends to become expensive.
4. Real-time systems
These systems are used when time requirements are very strict like missile systems, air traffic control systems, robots etc. Responce time of these systems is very critical.
eg
Railway reservation system, Satellite tracking system. 
5. Network  Operating System (NOS)
​
It is  a computer operating system (OS)  mainly designed to support workstations, PCs , older terminals that are connected on a local area network (LAN). NOS   enables multiple devices within a network to communicate and share resources with each other. However, a typical NOS no longer exists, as most  operating systems  have built-in network stacks that support a client-server model.
A NOS coordinates the activities of multiple computers across a network. This can include such devices as PCs, printers, file servers and databases connected to a local network. The role of the NOS is to provide basic network services and features that support multiple input requests simultaneously in a multiuser environment.
